description: ProofForge Level 1-2 curriculum: tactic arguments and two-step chains
design_principle: Each theorem requires exactly ONE new concept beyond Level 0 (single tactics). Level 1 = known tactic with argument. Level 2 = two-tactic chain where both tactics are already known.

tiers.name: level_1_tactic_args
tiers.description: Known tactics with specific arguments. The model knows simp/exact/apply but must learn to provide arguments.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l1_01 (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := by
theorem pf_l1_02 (n : Nat) : 0 + n = n := by
theorem pf_l1_03 (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a := by
theorem pf_l1_04 (a b c : Nat) : a + b + c = a + (b + c) := by
theorem pf_l1_05 (n : Nat) : n * 1 = n := by
theorem pf_l1_06 (n : Nat) : 1 * n = n := by
theorem pf_l1_07 (n : Nat) : n * 0 = 0 := by
theorem pf_l1_08 (a b : Nat) : a * b = b * a := by
theorem pf_l1_09 (n m : Nat) : n + m = m + n := by
theorem pf_l1_10 (n : Nat) : n - 0 = n := by

tiers.name: level_2_two_step_chains
tiers.description: Two-tactic chains. Both tactics are known from Level 0. The new skill is composition via semicolon or newline.

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l2_01 (p : Prop) : p -> p := by
theorem pf_l2_02 (p q : Prop) : p -> q -> p := by
theorem pf_l2_03 (p q : Prop) (hp : p) (hq : q) : p := by
theorem pf_l2_04 (p q : Prop) : p /\ q -> p := by
theorem pf_l2_05 (p q : Prop) : p /\ q -> q := by
theorem pf_l2_06 (p q : Prop) : p -> p \/ q := by
theorem pf_l2_07 (p q : Prop) : q -> p \/ q := by
theorem pf_l2_08 (p q : Prop) : p -> q -> p /\ q := by
theorems.known_proof: intro hp hq; exact And.intro hp hq

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l2_09 (n : Nat) : n = n + 0 := by
theorem pf_l2_10 (a b : Nat) (h : a = b) : b = a := by
theorem pf_l2_11 (a b c : Nat) (h : a = b) : a + c = b + c := by
theorem pf_l2_12 (p : Prop) : p -> ~~p := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h hn; exact hn h

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l2_13 (p q : Prop) : (p /\ q) -> (q /\ p) := by
theorems.known_proof: intro h; exact And.intro h.2 h.1

theorems.statement: theorem pf_l2_14 (f : Nat -> Nat) (a b : Nat) (h : a = b) : f a = f b := by
theorem pf_l2_15 (n : Nat) : 0 <= n := by
theorem pf_l2_16 (n : Nat) : n <= n + 1 := by
theorem pf_l2_17 (a b : Nat) (h : a <= b) : a <= b + 1 := by
theorem pf_l2_18 (p : Prop) : ~~p -> ~~p := by
theorem pf_l2_19 (p q : Prop) (h : p -> q) (hp : p) : q := by
theorem pf_l2_20 (n m : Nat) (h : n = m) : n + 1 = m + 1 := by
